rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Environmental pollution — air, water, and soil — is a major human-induced threat. Air pollution (SO2, NOx, CO, PM2.5, O3, CFCs) causes respiratory disease, acid rain, smog, and global warming; Kathmandu Valley's PM2.5 exceeds WHO limits ~10× in winter. Water pollution (domestic, industrial, agricultural) leads to eutrophication, O2 depletion, and disease.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Air pollutants: SO2, NOx, CO, PM2.5, O3, CFCs
Water pollutants: domestic waste, industrial effluent, agricultural runoff, oil
Soil pollutants: heavy metals, pesticides, plastics, industrial waste

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Acid rain (pH < 5.6) is caused by SO2 and NOx, NOT by CO2 alone.  ·  Ozone is beneficial in the STRATOSPHERE (blocks UV) but harmful at ground level (smog, air pollutant).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects clear sources, effects, and control measures for air, water, and soil pollution.  ·  Pesticides: types, effects, biomagnification, and resistance are a very common long-answer.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Air pollution: SO2 from coal plants, NOx from vehicles, PM2.5 from biomass stoves and dust in Kathmandu.  ·  Water pollution: domestic sewage in Bagmati and Karnali rivers; agricultural runoff (fertilisers, pesticides).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Biomagnification: toxin concentration INCREASES at higher trophic levels (e.g., DDT in fish-eating birds).  ·  Pesticide resistance: pests evolve resistance over time; higher doses are needed.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: List air pollutants and effects  ·  Explain water pollution

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Air = A-S-N-P (SO2, NOx, CO, PM2.5, O3, CFCs).  ·  Water = domestic + industrial + agricultural.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: List the sources and effects of air pollution.  ·  Explain water pollution (sources, effects, control).

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Describe the effects of soil pollution.  ·  Explain pesticides (types, effects, biomagnification, resistance).

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Air pollution (SO2, NOx, CO, PM2.5, O3, CFCs)  ·  Water pollution (domestic, industrial, agricultural)  ·  Soil pollution (heavy metals, pesticides, plastics)  ·  Pesticides (types, effects, biomagnification, resistance)

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Air pollution: SO2, NOx, CO, PM2.5, O3, CFCs; sources: industry, vehicles, biomass.  ·  Effects: respiratory disease, acid rain, smog, global warming, ozone depletion.  ·  Kathmandu Valley: PM2.5 exceeds WHO limits ~10× in winter.  ·  Water pollution: domestic, industrial, agricultural; effects: eutrophication, O2 depletion, disease.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: WHO guideline for PM2.5 is 10 µg/m³ (annual mean); Kathmandu Valley often exceeds 100 µg/m³ in winter.  ·  DDT (banned in many countries) biomagnifies up food chains; it caused eggshell thinning in raptors (eagles, falcons).

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: List control measures for air, water, and soil pollution.

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Give a Nepali example for each pollution type.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Soil pollution: heavy metals from industrial waste; pesticide residues in farmland.  ·  Pesticides: DDT (insecticide) biomagnifies in the food chain; non-target species (bees, fish) die.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: The main cause of acid rain is: → B  ·  Kathmandu Valley air pollution in winter is mainly due to: → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Environmental pollution: the addition of substances or energy to the environment at a rate that exceeds its capacity to dilute, degrade, or absorb them.  ·  Air pollution: SO2 (coal), NOx (vehicles), CO (incomplete combustion), PM2.5/PM10 (particulates), ozone (ground-level), CFCs; sources: industry, vehicles, power plants, biomass burning.  ·  Effects of air pollution: respiratory diseases (asthma, bronchitis), acid rain, smog, global warming, ozone depletion.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Acid rain  ·  Eutrophication  ·  Kathmandu PM2.5

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Control measures  ·  Biomagnification: toxin concentration INCREASES up the food chain  ·  Soil pollution: heavy metals, pesticides, plastics; effects: reduced fertility, food contamination.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Pesticides: insecticides, herbicides, fungicides, rodenticides; biomagnification, resistance, non-target death.  ·  Control: reduce emissions, renewable energy, tree planting, waste treatment, organic farming.  ·  Eutrophication: excess nutrients (N, P) → algal bloom → O2 depletion → fish kill.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: PM2.5 (fine particulates) are MORE harmful than PM10 because they penetrate deeper into the lungs.  ·  Control: tree planting, renewable energy, waste treatment, organic farming, international agreements.  ·  Kathmandu Valley air pollution (PM2.5) is a key Nepali application question.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Acid rain (SO2 + NOx) and ozone depletion (CFCs) are different processes.  ·  Biomagnification: give a DDT example (raptor eggshell thinning).  ·  Control measures: list 5+ for each pollution type.
